t:
Attorney and agent fees shall be paid out of the awards hereunder. No attorney or agent on account of services rendered in connection with each claim shall receive in excess of 20 per centum of the amount paid, any contract to the contrary notwithstanding.
Whoever violates the provisions of this Act shall be fined a sum not to exceed $1,000.

fable.w: This section only caps attorney and agent fees payable out of claim awards and sets a fine for violations. The tempting reading is that references to claims, attorneys and agents imply outside parties engaging with the government, but a fee limit on private representation is not consultation, a hearing, rulemaking, or a grant of a right to sue. No outside party is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: No attorney or agent on account of services rendered in connection with each claim shall receive in excess of 20 per centum of the amount paid

qwen_block.w: This section regulates the compensation of attorneys and agents representing claimants. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The interaction described is purely financial and regulatory regarding legal fees, not participatory in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Attorney and agent fees shall be paid out of the awards hereunder. No attorney or agent on account of services rendered in connection with each claim shall receive in excess of 20 per centum of the amount paid, any contract to the contrary notwithstanding.

opus.w: This section caps attorney and agent fees at 20 percent of claim awards and sets a fine for violations. Claimants and their representatives are outside the government, but pursuing a claim for an award is like applying for a benefit, which the definition excludes. The section does not require or allow consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body or a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: No attorney or agent on account of services rendered in connection with each claim shall receive in excess of 20 per centum of the amount paid, any contract to the contrary notwithstanding.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The text mentions claims, awards, attorneys and agents. That could suggest outside parties are taking part in a federal decision. It fails the definition: filing a claim for an award is like applying for a benefit. The section only caps fees and sets a fine. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section sets limits on attorney fees and establishes fines for violations. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The provisions are regulatory constraints and penalties, not mechanisms for public participation or advisory input.
qwen_chat.s: Attorney and agent fees shall be paid out of the awards hereunder. No attorney or agent on account of services rendered in connection with each claim shall receive in excess of 20 per centum of the amount paid, any contract to the contrary notwithstanding. Whoever violates the provisions of this Act shall be fined a sum not to exceed $1,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that limiting attorney fees or imposing fines involves some form of procedural interaction with outside parties (attorneys, claimants). However, this is merely a regulatory constraint on compensation and a penalty provision. It does not require the government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from outside parties before making a decision. The actors involved (attorneys, agents, violators) are not participating in the decision-making process; they are subject to the rules.
